channel.title: The Dig — Error correction route
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Error correction route preset. Today’s ranked reading list centers on silicon spin-qubit hardware and operational benchmarking: 2611.12850 proposes over-gate TiN stressors to enhance valley splitting in Si/SiGe wiggle-well dots, 2611.14114 offers a cloud-executed GHZ-fidelity benchmark that tests whether calibration data predict processor performance, and 2611.12217 maps how multi-dot configurations affect electron temperature and double-dot latching for initialization and readout. The skim-tier items broaden the context but sit further from current spin-qubit operation: 2611.13301 presents an MLIR-based fault-tolerant compiler, 2611.12779 a neutral-atom arbitrary two-qubit gate architecture, 2611.13371 silicon-spin qLDPC syndrome extraction with mobile ancillas, 2611.14422 a QRAM energetic-cost accounting method, and 2611.13796 an analog Rydberg-atom QAOA MaxCut study. No pay dirt today — 1 to skim.

item.title: Syndrome extraction for quantum LDPC codes in silicon: Distributed entanglement and mobile ancillas
item.description:
Skim new method — Mapping mobile-ancilla extraction onto a node lattice shortens the mean scheduled route for the [[144,12,12]] Gross code from 350 to 153 μm and reduces logical error rate up to 50-fold, beating distributed-singlet circuits across all sampled points unless two-qubit gate and readout errors fall below 4×10−4 to 5×10−4.

Grade 0.512 · 2.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation” · William Chow, Jonathan Baugh

Figure

Logical error rate per round versus shuttle dephasing probability psh across three bit-flip noise ratios, comparing original CAbLECAR, CAbLECAR remapped to the authors' node lattice, and distributed singlet gadgets (teleport and GHZ).

Asks

How do distributed-entanglement syndrome-extraction circuits compare to mobile ancilla transport for bivariate-bicycle codes on a shuttling-based silicon spin-qubit architecture?

Before

CAbLECAR mobile-ancilla scheduler on its original layout, which achieved a mean Gross-code route of 350 μm and was outperformed by teleportation under frequent transport bit flips.

But

Circuit-level memory simulations, open boundary conditions, non-faulty source undetectable fraction f=0 default, 12 rounds on [[144,12,12]] Gross code.

Tools

bivariate-bicycle code simulations · singlet fabric architecture · coherent electron shuttling · BP+OSD decoding

Code. https://github.com/KNFLWNF/singlet-fabric-qldpc

Abstract

Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can reduce the number of data qubits required per logical qubit, but their checks require long-range interactions on a planar device. We develop a singlet fabric for bivariate-bicycle codes on a silicon node network. Spin singlets are generated on shuttling lanes and distributed between nodes, where local operations consume them to measure non-local stabilizers. We construct two syndrome-extraction circuits, based on distributed GHZ states and ancilla teleportation, and evaluate them using hardware-constrained schedules and circuit-level memory simulations. We compare these circuits with CAbLECAR, which transports a mobile ancilla between the data qubits of each check. Teleportation can outperform CAbLECAR on its original layout when transport includes spin flips as well as dephasing. Placing the mobile ancilla on our node lattice, however, shortens the mean scheduled route for the [[144,12,12]] Gross code from 350 to 153 μm and lowers its logical error rate up to 50-fold in the sampled bit-flip regime. Direct transport then achieves a lower logical error rate than either singlet circuit at every sampled Gross-code point. With frequent transport bit flips, the GHZ circuit overtakes direct transport once two-qubit gate and readout errors fall below about 4-5×10⁻⁴, roughly half the value assumed here. Fixing the ancilla's data-visit order reveals a trade-off between shorter routes and the correlated errors produced by ancilla faults. Source heralding improves both singlet circuits, whereas phase purification helps the GHZ circuit only above a noise-dependent crossover and worsens teleportation throughout. These results show that the physical layout and interaction order can be as consequential as the choice of extraction circuit, and that cleaner entangled resources do not necessarily produce a more reliable logical memory.
